summary: The biggest new problem is the IBTR note, the strongest of the three picks. On the 15 Oct Treasury curve, the ten payments cost $298,624 using the team's own method (the same one that gives the 6 Oct figures of $293,448 and 22.7bp). That leaves only $1,376, or 4.7bp, of room. Long yields have already fallen the "about 0.2 percentage points" that the note names. MODEL: about a 1-in-4 to 1-in-3 chance that the ladder costs more than $300,000 on the day the team takes its figure. So the reflection must use one fixed date (the 20 Oct curve) and have logic ready for both outcomes, and the IPS must change its stale "$292,000" figure and its "2027 leftover first" backstop. Even if the line is crossed, the October rule's trade at WInS scale stays below the kit's $2,500 minimum unless yields fall about another 18bp (fixed-floor reading) or 69bp (IPS V5 reading). So holding remains the rule's answer: restate or retire trigger B on the WInS basis and log each check. IBTR, IBTM and VT still meet every hard requirement: real filled trades, notes under 300 characters, plain ASCII. But together they never mention liquidity (one of Wharton's named themes). They also read as one burst of buying unless each reflection shows a different kind of decision: a rule set in advance, a change forced by the 6 Oct email, and a choice among alternatives (the 5 Oct VT "copout" debate, whose outcome is still unrecorded). Wharton's own example note assumes a gradual glide path, so the team must say in plain words why it locked the payments early. Eleven trades and "hold" is backed by Wharton's own text, but WInS shows no monitoring, so a dated decision log is the evidence; adding notes to old trades later would look retro-fitted. Wharton's live Rules page names only the IPS and Final Report for Top 50 selection, so the TNA should be correct and consistent but time-boxed. Still unseen: the Week-One email (the only possible activity rule) and the SMApply TNA form, where "Mark as Complete" is not the same as submitting.

findings.title: IBTR note's threshold almost used up: 4.7bp of room on 15 Oct
findings.problem: The filled IBTR note says the first $300,000 buys all ten payments unless yields fall more than about 0.2 points. Re-run with the team's method (end-date sizing, curve rolled to 1 Jan 2027): $293,448 / 22.7bp on 6 Oct, $295,988 / 13.9bp on 14 Oct, $298,624 / 4.7bp ($1,376) on 15 Oct. Long yields are down 0.20 points since 6 Oct (20y 5.68 to 5.48). MODEL random walk at 2026 volatility (4.71bp a day): cost above $300k on 20 Oct about 28%, on 22 Oct about 33%, on 6 Nov about 40%. A reflection quoting the 15 Oct brief's '0.16' or saying 'not triggered' may be false when judged, in the strongest pick.
